title: Mysterious Object In Everett Again - Learn About Panthalassa | My Everett News
excerpt: Back in 2024, readers noticed a strange object being transported to Everett. It turned out to be a "renewable energy buoy" built by Panthalassa.
content:
Mysterious object being transported through the Puget Sound towards Everett.

Back in 2024, readers noticed a strange object being transported to Everett. It turned out to be a “renewable energy buoy” built by Panthalassa.

Over the past two days several people spotted another mysterious object being transported to Everett. Rumors started flying in. Was it a rocket? A space laser? A giant baby bottle?

Again, it was a Panthalassa buoy, but this time it is a renewable energy data center.

2024 picture of Panthalassa test renewable energy buoy in Everett (top). 2026 picture of Panthalassa test AI data center buoy in Everett (bottom).

In May, 2026, Oregon-based Panthalassa received a $140 million round led by Peter Thiel and others for “wave-powered AI.”

The new funding from the controversial PayPal and Palantir co-founder allows Panthalassa to finish building its pilot manufacturing facility in Vancouver.

The name comes from 250 million years ago when much of the Earth was covered by a superocean known as Panthalassa.

Energy and cooling are two of the greatest challenges for modern data centers.

Panthalassa’s technology pairs wave power generated by massive floating orbs with onsite AI computing. The ocean provides the cooling and the data is transported by via low-Earth-orbit satellites.

Panthalassa’s renewable energy AI data center at the Port of Everett Tuesday.

In August, Panthalassa took additional investment from a Korean cloud firm called Naver. The undisclosed round brings Panthalassa’s value to $2 billion. The company will be raising funds again in 2027.

We believe the object spotted this week in Everett is “Ocean-3.” It will be placed somewhere in the Pacific Ocean to demonstrate the scalability of their AI data center platform.

If successful, they will scale up manufacturing to start building gigafactories.
